sn3.15:1.3: “King Ajātasattu of Magadha, son of the princess of Videha, it seems, has mobilized an army of four divisions and marched against me to Kāsi.”
sn3.15:4.1: “Here, sir, King Ajātasattu of Magadha, son of the princess of Videha, mobilized an army of four divisions and marched to Kāsi to attack King Pasenadi of Kosala.
sn3.15:4.2: When King Pasenadi heard of this, sir:
sn3.15:4.3: ‘King Ajātasattu of Magadha, son of the princess of Videha, it seems, has mobilized an army of four divisions and marched against me to Kāsi.’
sn3.15:4.4: Then, sir, King Pasenadi of Kosala mobilized an army of four divisions and marched to Kāsi to defend it against King Ajātasattu of Magadha, son of the princess of Videha.
sn3.15:4.5: Then, sir, King Ajātasattu of Magadha, son of the princess of Videha, and King Pasenadi of Kosala met in battle.
sn3.15:4.6: And in that battle, sir, King Pasenadi of Kosala defeated King Ajātasattu of Magadha, son of the princess of Videha, and captured him alive.
sn3.15:4.7: Then, sir, King Pasenadi of Kosala thought this:
sn3.15:4.8: ‘Even though I’ve never betrayed this King Ajātasattu of Magadha, son of the princess of Videha, he betrayed me. Still, he is my nephew.
sn3.15:4.9: Now that I’ve vanquished all of the elephant troops, cavalry, chariots, and infantry of King Ajātasattu of Magadha, son of the princess of Videha, why don’t I let him loose with just his life?’”
sn3.15:5.1: “Then, sir, King Pasenadi of Kosala vanquished all of the elephant troops, cavalry, chariots, and infantry of King Ajātasattu of Magadha, son of the princess of Videha, and let him loose with just his life.”
